Slow handover house rules for treat supplies
This page helps new colleagues see what is expected

This page explains the safe handling of treat supplies at the Companion Animal Travel Desk and why careful control matters. Treats can calm a pet, support a smooth handover, and reassure a worried passenger, but only when they are issued in the right manner. You must keep supplies clean, sealed, and separate from personal items. Open packets should never be left where a pet or passenger can reach them without supervision.

When preparing for boarding, check the supply label, confirm the package is intact, and place it where crew can access it without delay. If a traveler asks for a snack for an animal, respond in a calm and respectful manner and verify that the item is suitable before offering it. Do not improvise with unknown food, shared packaging, or anything that has been exposed to contamination. Report any sign of damage, loss, or mix-up at once so the senior coordinator can decide the next step.

<<FACT F069>> Keep that instruction in mind while handling crates and related supplies. Use the same care when you brief the crew and when you receive items back after transfer. If a pet such as Basil appears unsettled, maintain a steady tone and follow the approved sequence without rushing.

<<FACT F074>> Apply that rule before you release any animal for travel. If a passenger seems uncertain, explain only the approved process and avoid casual promises. Good service depends on accuracy, quiet attention, and a consistent handover.

Remember: handle treats carefully, verify every detail, and keep the pet's welfare first.
